paragraphs: Children in care in Wrexham are looked after by Foster Wales Wrexham, the fostering service of Wrexham County Borough Council, and by the agencies listed on this page. The council says there are children of every age in the county borough who need a family, from babies and toddlers to teenagers, brothers and sisters who need to stay together, and young parents with their babies.

Foster Wales Wrexham recruits several kinds of carer: kinship carers who look after a child they already know, general foster carers, therapeutic carers, parent and baby carers, When I am Ready carers, and more experienced professional carers for children with complex needs. The council has said it wants more carers to foster with the local authority. In February 2023 it approved a substantial rise in what it pays its carers, with higher weekly allowances, skills payments for specialist carers, school uniform payments and a council tax reduction; ask the team for the rates that apply now.

Wrexham's carers are part of a Wales-wide change. The Welsh Government says that from 1 April 2026 new fostering providers in Wales must be not-for-profit, and existing profit-making providers cannot add new services. Whichever service you choose, speak to two or three, compare training, out-of-hours support and pay, and ask how the change affects them.
